skill.name: skill-harvest
skill.description: Review Claude Code session history to identify reusable methods, find overlooked installed skills, and guide evidence-based skill creation and publication.
skill.summary: Turn recurring session patterns into tested skills and targeted reminders.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: Most static findings identify harmless Markdown formatting, documented local skill paths, or public GitHub inventory requests. Confirmed output risks concern unredacted private digests and spreadsheet formulas in CSV metadata; a separate finding covers unpinned npm execution. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or covert exfiltration; publication and hook installation explicitly require user approval.

remediation.issue: Private human prompts are copied into persistent digests without secret redaction or explicit restrictive permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets before writing digests, restrict directory and file permissions, and provide project selection and a documented retention policy.

remediation.issue: Session-controlled metadata is exported to CSV without protection against spreadsheet formulas.
remediation.suggestion: Neutralize formula-leading characters in every exported text cell and test titles beginning with equals, plus, minus, at-sign, and control characters.

remediation.issue: Market searches invoke an unpinned npm package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed, pinned CLI version and obtain approval before downloading or executing third-party packages.

content.user_title: Discover Reusable Skills in Your Session History
content.value_statement: Useful methods and overlooked installed skills are scattered across past conversations. Skill Harvest organizes Claude Code history into evidence for skill discovery, testing, and approved publication.
actual_capabilities: Generate Markdown digests and a CSV index from recent Claude Code session logs without modifying the source transcripts.
Record human prompt excerpts, loaded skills, tool counts, session dates, and working directories.
Prefilter overlooked installed skills by matching quoted trigger phrases against human requests.
Guide evidence-based candidate selection and comparison with public skill listings.
Guide three-prompt comparisons with and without a proposed skill before approved publication.
Provide an optional prompt hook that suggests up to three installed skills using configurable phrase rules.
limitations: The scripts target Claude Code logs and directories; native Codex history ingestion is not implemented.
Human-turn detection depends on specific log fields, and phrase matching requires manual relevance review.
This is batch analysis, not continuous observation or guaranteed automatic delivery to other sessions.
Digest generation does not automatically redact secrets, and search or publication steps require external tools and network access.

use_cases.title: Find Repeated Development Methods
use_cases.description: Review recurring requests and corrections across sessions to identify reusable skills supported by independent evidence.

use_cases.title: Improve Installed Skill Usage
use_cases.description: Find installed skills that were not loaded during relevant work, then review targeted reminders before enabling them.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Skill Publication Candidates
use_cases.description: Compare candidate methods with public alternatives, test three past prompts, and prepare sanitized materials for explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my last seven days of Claude Code sessions for repeated methods. Keep results private and do not install or publish anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find Overlooked Installed Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my recent session digests with installed skills. Show likely missed matches with dates and evidence, and manually reject irrelevant matches.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the strongest candidate using independent session evidence and public alternatives. Use generic search terms without private data and request approval before package execution.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Skill and Reminder Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft the qualifying skill, compare three sanitized prompts with and without it, and propose reminder rules. Wait for approval before installation or publication.

best_practices: Use a private output directory, review digests for secrets, and neutralize formula-like CSV cells before spreadsheet use.
Count independent evidence, verify heuristic matches manually, and compare public alternatives using generic search terms.
Approve package execution, hook settings, and each publication separately after reviewing the proposed changes.
anti_patterns: Treating repeated copies of one broadcast message as independent evidence for a new skill.
Publishing transcript excerpts or assuming generated digests have already removed confidential information.
Installing every matched skill or enabling reminder hooks without reviewing relevance and settings changes.

faq.question: Does it support Codex session history?
faq.answer: The workflow may inform Codex skill work, but the bundled scripts parse Claude Code logs and use Claude directories.

faq.question: Does it watch every conversation live?
faq.answer: No. It processes saved sessions in batches and describes incremental reruns. The optional hook only suggests skills for incoming prompts.

faq.question: Does it change the original transcripts?
faq.answer: The reader opens source logs for reading and writes separate digests and an index. The instructions prohibit modifying transcript files.

faq.question: Are private details removed automatically?
faq.answer: No. Digests include human prompt excerpts and metadata. Review and protect these files before sharing them or using them in external workflows.

faq.question: Will it publish or install hooks automatically?
faq.answer: The instructions require approval for each publication and before hook settings changes. Local skill installation is part of the proposed workflow.

faq.question: What qualifies a candidate for building?
faq.answer: Candidates need repeated independent evidence, a reusable method, a market gap, testable prompts, and no required private data. Public candidates must also generalize.
